newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium prices to rise by 10 pct in 97-MacQuarie.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium prices to rise by 10 pct in 97-MacQuarie.

text.p: The aluminium market will move into deficit in 1997, boosting the average cash price on the London Metal exchange by about 10 percent to $1,665 per tonne, MacQuarie Equities said in a report.
A market deficit of 150,000 to 200,000 tonnes, although relatively small, would bring stocks to about 7-1/2 weeks of consumption, it said.
"This is still above the critical level for aluminium stocks (6-6-1/2 weeks), but should be sufficient to lift prices," MacQuarie said.
A surplus of 290,000 tonnes and an average LME cash price of $1,505 is forecast for 1996.
Demand has been hit this year by massive destocking by consumers and semi-fabricators, which has tapered off in the final quarter.
Now that demand is starting to reflect underlying consumption, strong growth is likely, particularly in the first half of 1997.
"Our forecast of 4.1 percent demand growth in 1997 could well turn out to be an underestimate," the report said.

The biggest question mark for the market is the supply side. Nearly one million tonnes per year of aluminium smelting capacity remains idle and it is likely to remain off-line throughout most of 1997.
"However, a premature restart would be enough to bring the market into balance or even into surplus, preventing prices from recovering."
Exports from the former Soviet Union have shifted from semis to primary, and domestic consumption has hit a new low.
"But if domestic consumption begins to recover in 1997, primary exports to the West could fall sharply," the report said.
